prompt:
You review onboarding copy for a desktop pet app whose users may include children. For each change,
read every user-facing text and decide whether any of it, in any wording, does one of these:
- mentions price, money, discounts, gifts, free extras, memberships or paying
- suggests skipping, postponing or getting around a step (especially sign in)
- creates urgency or scarcity, or says others are taking the pets
- guilt-trips or shames someone for declining or for their choice
- asks for personal information about the user (name, contact, location, age, accounts)
- otherwise pressures or tricks the user
Ordinary friendly copy is fine ("Feel free to look around", "No rush, take your time"). Signing in is a
required step, so asking people to sign in on the sign-in step, or saying their pet is kept safe in their
account, is fine; asking for details about the person is not.
Return JSON {"verdicts": [{"index": i, "fair": true or false, "problem": short or null}]}

Texts per change:
0: ["Choose Companion Trait"]
1: ["Your Journey Begins", "Review the world of companion desktop pets before choosing your path.", "Continue to Path Selection", "Every companion brings unique magic to your desktop."]
2: []
3: ["Preparing companion assets..."]
4: ["Signing in with your original account restores all your previous pets and progress automatically."]
5: ["Your pet is being crafted in the background. You can minimize this window; we will alert you as soon as your companion is ready!"]
6: ["Don't worry about picking the wrong path—you can customize your pet's look and traits in the next steps!"]
7: ["Interacting With Your Desktop Pet", "Click and drag your pet anywhere on screen. Right-click to open settings, chat, or send your companion to rest.", "Got It!"]
8: ["If photo upload fails or looks unexpected, high-quality companion presets will be provided automatically."]
9: ["Welcome to Your Desktop Companion!", "Your pet is now active on your desktop. Complete these final setup steps to get started."]
